March came around again, and the family gathered at the old house on the hill. Gifts had been carefully assembled in the weeks before — wrapped in colored paper, ribbons tied just so. Candles were lit one by one, and the cake stood waiting on the long oak table. Everyone present that evening felt the warmth of celebration, another year marked, another year of being together. The presents were opened slowly, each one drawing soft laughter or a quiet thank-you. By the end of the night, the family sat around the table together, full and tired and glad to have come.
